name: Iran nuclear programme
value: IAEA access to bombed sites still unagreed
summary: Iran holds about 441 kg at 60%, per the IAEA; inspector access to bombed sites rests on a Qatari plan not yet agreed
state: AP reported on 6 Nov that Iran holds about 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60%, per the IAEA, and will not negotiate on nuclear issues until the US meets its conditions. A Qatari plan would have Iran admit IAEA inspectors to bombed sites as the US lifts its blockade (AP). A senior Iranian official told Reuters that a nuclear proposal sent via Qatar depends on seven US demands being met (Times of Israel). Israeli Defence Minister Katz said on 8 Nov that Iran is trying to renew efforts to obtain nuclear weapons, which Iran has long denied (The New Arab). No strike on a nuclear site was found in reporting to 9 Nov.
for_you: No direct public action follows from this signal. FCDO travel advice is the reference for anyone in Iran or nearby states. Stalled verification means outside estimates of Iran's stockpile and sites carry more uncertainty than usual.
rubric_hit: Watch: enrichment at 60% (about 440.9 kg, per IAEA via AP) and inspector access curtailed; no strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or weaponisation evidence found

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.

rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
